D.tier: Queued, roster and office levers only

D.t: David Jolly trails by 3.8 and wins 25% of simulations. Closing it takes about 169,009 voters switching sides, or 338,018 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.6 and D +4.3. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.8. Your best recent poll is Change Research at D +0.8; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +9.1. 21 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 213,428 votes; Orange, a projected net 90,359 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 76,777 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +0.7, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +7.4, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.7, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +5.1, 4.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, David Jolly runs furthest behind in Osceola, Collier, Lee. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 51 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; White voters, 69% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 47 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points.
The forecast's worst groups for David Jolly: Immigration voters 19 to 79, Incomes $125K and up 38 to 60, Midsize counties 40 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.0M cash against $44.0M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 38% of the 4,717,903 ballots in Florida so far, against 41% for the other party. That is 7.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 2.0 points away from David Jolly. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $44.0M in the bank against $6.0M for David Jolly.

R.t: Byron Donalds leads by 3.8 in the forecast and wins 75% of simulations. The cushion is about 338,018 votes; a one point swing is about 44,711 voters changing sides.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Lee, a projected net 82,332 votes; Collier, a projected net 56,261 votes; Marion, a projected net 42,575 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +0.7, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +7.4, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.7, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +5.1, 4.4% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Byron Donalds runs furthest behind in Pinellas, Hernando, Broward. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

The forecast's worst groups for Byron Donalds: Black voters 19 to 79, Independents 26 to 70, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 33 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$44.0M cash against $6.0M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
